summary.text: Aridity is the condition of regions with low yearly precipitation, higher temperatures and limited water, and such areas make up about 43% of the world's available land.
Where arid regions lie at any time depends largely on the general circulation of the atmosphere, and that circulation shifts significantly as the climate changes.
Land use can add to aridity by drawing more on soil water, and a December 2024 UNCCD report found more than three-quarters of Earth's land has become permanently drier.

items.prompt: A farming valley grows hotter over the years while its yearly rain drops and its wells run low. Which way is its climate heading?
items.explain: Low yearly precipitation, higher temperatures and limited water are the marks of aridity.

items.prompt: Roughly what share of the world's available land is made up of arid areas?
items.explain: Arid areas make up approximately 43% of total global available land, far more than most people guess.

items.prompt: What mostly decides where on Earth the dry regions sit at any given time?

options.label: Which plants happen to grow there
The age of the bedrock underneath
Earth's distance from the Sun that year

items.explain: The distribution of aridity is largely the result of the general circulation of the atmosphere.

items.prompt: Rainfall in a region stays exactly the same, but its land is switched to uses that pull far more water out of the ground. What can happen?

options.label: Nothing, since only rain sets dryness
The region can become more arid
The rain will rise to match the use

items.explain: Changes in land use can increase demands on soil water and so increase aridity, even with no change in rain.

items.prompt: Warming over the next few decades could turn the Nile Basin from semi-arid into arid. What would that most directly shrink?
items.explain: Such a shift would significantly reduce the land that can be used for agriculture.

items.prompt: Many regions have dried out in recent decades. What did a December 2024 UNCCD report conclude about those drier climates?

options.label: They will recover within ten years
They are limited to existing deserts
They will not go back to how they were
They are a short seasonal swing

items.explain: The report found the drier climates now affecting vast regions will not return to how they were, calling the change permanent.
